episode.title: Ep. 202 — History doesn't have to repeat itself in Afghanistan

persons.name: Jerry Dunleavy
persons.role: Guest; former senior investigator, House Foreign Affairs Committee Afghanistan withdrawal investigation (resigned Aug 2024); co-author of 'Kabul: The Untold Story of Biden's Fiasco'

mentions.quote: He was the senior investigator for the House Foreign Affairs Committee investigation of the withdrawal from Afghanistan. And yesterday, Jerry dropped his resignation letter on Twitter.

persons.name: Will Selber
persons.role: Co-host; retired USAF Middle East foreign area officer, four Afghanistan tours, Bulwark contributor; testified to HFAC alongside Gen. Sami Sadat

mentions.quote: my co-host today is Will Selber ... a retired Middle East foreign area officer
I testified, you know, in front of the committee, obviously alongside General Sammy Sadat

persons.name: Joe Biden
persons.role: US President; 'go-to-zero' order kicked off the withdrawal cascade; failed to enforce Doha conditions

mentions.quote: Ultimately, President Biden's decision, his go-to-zero order, his lack of planning, him not making the people under him do their jobs

persons.name: Kamala Harris
persons.role: US Vice President; 'last person in the room', supported withdrawal decision

mentions.quote: Vice President Harris, now the Democratic nominee was the last person in the room, according to her. She supported this.

persons.name: Mark Milley
persons.role: Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff 2019-23; overstated ANDSF at 325,000-350,000; got hearing title changed

mentions.quote: General Millie trying to say that the Afghan military and police forces were 325,000 to 350,000 strong, which anybody could tell you that was never true
General Millie, called Chairman McCall and said, hey, this, I don't like this hearing title ... and Chairman McCall changed the hearing title

persons.name: Kenneth McKenzie
persons.role: CENTCOM commander 2019-22; reportedly turned down Taliban offer on 15 Aug 2021 to let US secure Kabul

mentions.quote: General McKenzie. His decision, it seems like on the spot to turn down the Taliban's offer, even on August 15th, an offer from the Taliban to stay out of Kabul, to let the U.S. military come in, secure the city

persons.name: Michael McCaul
persons.role: Chairman, House Foreign Affairs Committee; ran the Afghanistan withdrawal investigation

mentions.quote: Chairman McCall had agreed to allow the two men to come in together only in a classified space

persons.name: Zalmay Khalilzad
persons.role: Architect of the Doha agreement; retained by Biden in 2021 to broker Taliban-dominated power-sharing (60-40, 70-30); told HFAC AQIS 'doesn't exist anymore'; treated as friendly witness

mentions.quote: all evidence indicated that Zal is for Zal ... the chief investigator took a selfie with Zalmei Calaisade after the testimony
He told us behind closed doors that al-Qaeda in the Indian subcontinent doesn't exist anymore ... this is a psychotic lie to tell
these deals were Taliban, 50-50 Taliban, 60-40 Taliban ... 70-30 Taliban? ... This is what Zao was pushing for. This is what the Biden administration was pushing for.
Wotan furush, that's what they call him ... He sold out his country.

persons.name: Abdul Rahman al-Logari
persons.role: ISIS-K suicide bomber who carried out the Abbey Gate attack; captured 2017 in joint CIA-India operation, held at Parwan prison, freed by Taliban Aug 2021
persons.status_detail: died in Abbey Gate suicide bombing, 26 Aug 2021

mentions.quote: Abdulrahman al-Lagri is the ISIS-K bomber. He was captured in a joint CIA India operation in 2017 ... imprisoned in Parwan prison at Bagram Air Base. when the Taliban took Bagram ... they freed thousands of prisoners, Taliban, Al-Qaeda, and ISIS-K

persons.name: Kabir Aidi
persons.role: ISIS-K facilitator supplying suicide vests and explosives from Nangarhar into Kabul; killed in US strike day after Abbey Gate
persons.status_detail: killed in US strike in Nangarhar, 27 Aug 2021

mentions.quote: the strike that we carried out the day after the Abbey Gate bombing against a terrorist named Kabir Ayydi, who was supplying suicide vests and explosives from Nangar province into Kabul

persons.name: Christopher Donahue
persons.role: US Army general commanding 82nd Airborne at Kabul airport; with Vasely denied a pre-Abbey Gate strike request due to Taliban objection

mentions.quote: his request was denied by Vasily and Donahue due to a negative response from the Taliban

persons.name: Peter Vasely
persons.role: US Navy rear admiral commanding US Forces Afghanistan-Forward during the evacuation; never called by HFAC

mentions.quote: military commanders like General Vasili or in front of the committee?
has not brought in the people who would potentially know the answer to them, Vasley, Donahue, Sullivan

persons.role: US Marine Lt. Col. on the ground at Kabul airport; interviewed by HFAC in classified setting with no transcript

key_claims: The HFAC Afghanistan investigation squandered aligned political conditions by refusing to call key witnesses (Vasely, Donahue, Sullivan, Nuland, Sherman, Jacobson) and treating Milley, McKenzie and Khalilzad with kid gloves.

The Abbey Gate bomber, Abdul Rahman al-Logari, was a 2017 CIA-India capture freed by the Taliban from Parwan prison; DoD's claim the attack was 'not preventable' even had prisoners stayed jailed is 'insanity'.
A US strike request on an ISIS-K location days before Abbey Gate was denied by Vasely and Donahue because of Taliban objection; the Taliban refused US requests to raid ISIS-K sites in Kabul.
McKenzie rejected on the spot a 15 Aug 2021 Taliban offer to let the US secure Kabul for the evacuation.
Khalilzad is 'for Zal': he pushed Kabul to accept a 60-40/70-30 Taliban-dominated government in 2021 and told HFAC that AQIS no longer exists, a 'psychotic lie'; Afghans call him Watan Furush.
Ghani's flight was cowardice but it foiled the Biden administration's plan for a 'peaceful transition' to a Taliban-dominated government.
Milley's 325,000-350,000 ANDSF figure was never true; generals gave some correct strategic advice but misread the ground.
Taliban–al-Qaeda alliance remains very strong and AQ is growing in Afghanistan.
